title: Queue Priority Under Alternating Aggression

data_provenance.text: The source is a locally authored pedagogical message fixture, not data from a real security or venue.
The ladder and tape are deterministic consequences of replaying the supplied source fixture messages through the FIFO exchange.

historical_context.text: This pack validates exact-message teaching architecture with alternating aggressive buys and sells around a two-sided book.

learning_objectives: Relate aggressive order flow to FIFO queue depletion.
Decide when crossing a displayed spread is justified by available liquidity.
Separate exact source-message replay from claims about a real historical market.

event.text: A fixed pedagogical message sequence alternated aggressive buying, cancellation, and aggressive selling.

market_context.text: Displayed queues at 100.01 and 99.99 absorbed the first aggressive orders before deeper prices traded.

what_happened_next.text: The replay produced six FIFO trades and ended with the surviving source orders at their exact replayed prices.

why_session_matters.text: It makes queue priority, spread crossing, and source-message causality inspectable without adding synthetic orders.

known_limitations: The source is not real-market data and cannot support claims about an actual instrument or venue.
The fixture supplies order and trade messages but does not claim source-provided full book snapshots.
The lesson is a five-second architecture fixture, not a representative trading day.
training_questions: Did displayed liquidity disappear before the next price traded?
Was crossing the spread justified by the source-visible queue?
Which source order held FIFO priority at each trade?
